name: Tri-Scam
text: [overview] Stay on that ice, then step left into a snowy, low-angle corner.

name: Easy Gully
text: [overview] Begin with easy snow through the trees and, depending on how much snow lies there, loose rock, up to the point where the snow steepens.
[overview] Pitch two covers steeper snow onto easy ice of grade 1 to 2-, and the gully is left via the right side to more rappel anchors.

name: H&D (Hunter and Dog) Gully
text: [overview] Ascend the steeply angled snow and set up a belay.
[overview] Both choices also involve snow of moderate steepness.

name: Cass’ Gully
text: [overview] A snow gully for the most part, running beside an enormous rock buttress.

name: Hourglass Chute
text: [approach] Take the Profanity trail to roughly the 4,100-foot level, then traverse right (north) beneath the east face of the Chin, following the base of the rock face to the fan of snow at the bottom of the chute.
[approach] a steep snow slope funnels into a narrow couloir before opening onto a moderate slope.
[approach] It needs good snow cover to fill in, and is best after a hard freeze at dawn.
[approach] Carry an ice axe and avoid it on powder days because of avalanche risk.
